items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I remember one night at a session in Jimmy Ryans when Tommy's brother, Jimmy Dorsey jammed with me and some other cats, so now I had met the two famous brothers.

ctx.x: Another night, I met two movie stars who were in Paris either on vacation or to make a film. I was never a nosey Joe or curious as a cat, so I did not ask them their reason for being in the city. They were Shirley Winters and John Garfield. John was a heavy jucier and he slept in a chair almost from the time he came in until the night was finished for us. I had seen him in many films but had never seen or heard anything about Shirley Winters, who was a starlet then. She was a vivacious girl who liked to dance and…

We also had a visit of Tommy Dorsey one night. I had seen Tommy and heard some of his orchestras in the Apple, but had never met him. Someone asked him to sit in with us and although he did not have his trombone with him, he tried the one that Charles Huss had and found out that it was a good instrument, so he played a couple of numbers with us. I told him that I played in Sy Oliver's orchestra before I came to France and he was quite well pleased to hear that, as Sy had been his arranger for a few years. There…

At times I would have a gig out of town for which I would inform the artistic director of the club, whose name was Guy Masse. In March, 1952, on a certain date, I was engaged by Willy de Cort, president of the Belgium Hot Club to play a concert at the Galeries des Beaux Arts in Brussels. Don Byas and Art Simmen were also engaged for this deal. I don't remember the rest of the musicians. Another organisation had organised a concert with Sidney Bechet and as Willy was the first and biggest organiser or jazz…
